To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the generating functional Ψ[j] of the correlation functions for the solutions of a Langevin equation with constraints coincides with the partition function of a field theory; and (ii) the generating functional of correlation functions for the dynamics of the freely jointed chain can be expressed in terms of the generating functional of a field theory.

the dynamics of a freely-jointed chain in the continuous (long chain) limit can be described by the nonlinear sigma model and that this description can be connected to the stochastic dynamics of a chain of beads connected by links of fixed lengths.
the path integral of the continuous limit of a freely jointing chain coincides with the path integral of a constrained Langeving equation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of an ideal chain, i.e. of a chain whose links are freely jointed.
the dynamics of an ensemble of beads connected together in a chain.
the dynamics of a system of beads connected by links of fixed lengths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics of a freely joined chain is described by a nonlinear sigma model whose solutions are the trajectories of the stochastic process defined by a constrained Langevin dynamics.

the generating functional of a stochastic process with nonholonomic constraints is the generating functional of another stochastic process without constraints, which is obtained by a suitable projection of the first stochastic process.

, if the dynamics of a chain is described as the diffusion of a set of beads connected together, the Langevin equation governing the motion of the chain contains nonholonomic conditions, i.e. it is a constrained Langevin process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of an ideal chain in the presence of a solvent is governed by a constrained Langevin dynamics.
the Langevin equation for a constrained stochastic process can be derived from the path integral for a field theory with nonholonomic constraints.
the dynamics of the chain in the continuous case is equivalent to a stochastic process in which the Brownian motion takes place in a nonlinear manifold.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the continuous limit, the Langevin equation governing the dynamics of the chain is the one obtained by constraining the stochastic dynamics of the nonlinear sigma model to satisfy the topological condition of inextensibility.
the dynamics of the freely jointed chain can be understood in terms of a Langevin equation, which is constrained in such a way that the links of the chain do not change their lengths.

the Langevin equation for a chain with nonholonomic constraints can be used to study the dynamics of a freely-jointed chain in the continuous case, and that this equation can be derived by a suitable discretization of the field theory.
